memo:
EdgeHound Performance Review — 24 June 2026

Portfolio is down 15% from inception ($10K → $8,501 equity), with $1,609 realized losses across 205 closed trades. The core SHORT_FAVORITE engine on high-priced sports markets remains the only validated edge (70% win rate, 90% CI 63–77%, n=121), yet the engine's aggregate PnL is -$478 — a paradox explained by stake sizing anomalies and stop-loss events dragging realized returns despite a strong win rate. Inspection of recent trades reveals the core problem: the bot is occasionally putting $150–$500 stakes on individual markets (Cleveland, Jordan/Algeria, Mets, Twins) while the Kelly multiplier should be producing much smaller positions at current bank size. The $450 ELITE_FOLLOW on Colombia/DR Congo that closed at zero and the $500 ELITE_FOLLOW on Jordan/Algeria are concerning size outliers relative to a $8,500 equity base.

MOMENTUM (-$1,019, 8/21 wins) and SMART_CONSENSUS (-$385, 0/1) remain disabled — correct. VOLUME_SPIKE is marginally profitable (+$190) with a 40% win rate, suggesting it adds noise but occasionally catches moves. ELITE_FOLLOW is near breakeven (+$82, 48% win rate) — insufficient edge to justify $450–$500 single-trade stakes.

Immediate priority: reduce kellyMult slightly to compress outlier stake sizes, and cap maxEventExposure to limit single-market concentration. No engine changes warranted. Brier score of 0.24 indicates moderate but not strong calibration.
observations: SHORT_FAVORITE sports validated (70% WR, n=121) but aggregate PnL -$478 — stop-loss events and mid-sized losses on individual games eroding wins
ELITE_FOLLOW generating $450–$500 single-trade stakes on markets with no validated edge (48% WR) — largest single source of drawdown risk
MOMENTUM remains correctly disabled: -$1,019 on 21 trades, 38% win rate
VOLUME_SPIKE marginally positive (+$190, 40% WR) — borderline but not enough to disable yet, n=20
Brier 0.24 — calibration mediocre; model's pPredicted values (0.60–0.72) are not matching realized outcomes well enough to justify aggressive sizing
Open positions show two large stakes: $500 on Twins (entry 0.845, now 0.965 — likely near resolution) and $400 on Royals (entry 0.935, now 0.965)
Wallet 'aenews2' scoring 44% win rate (6W/8L) — ELITE_FOLLOW copying this wallet is destroying value; 'denizz' (0.8 score) should be prioritized if engine stays on
15% equity drawdown from start warrants defensive posture until edge is re-demonstrated
changesApplied: pMin capped at 0.6 (high-prior engines off; 0.61 would block all trades)
changeReasoning: Reducing kellyMult from 0.15 to 0.13 and maxEventExposure from $750 to $600 to prevent the outsized ELITE_FOLLOW and SHORT_FAVORITE stakes ($400–$500) that are punching above their validated edge. pMin raised marginally to 0.61 to filter marginal SHORT_FAVORITE entries. maxExposure trimmed to 0.35 to reflect 15% drawdown and the need for capital preservation while edge is rebuilt. No engine changes: SHORT_FAVORITE remains the only validated engine; ELITE_FOLLOW kept on due to borderline-positive PnL but will be reviewed if wallet-copy behavior keeps generating large losing trades. MOMENTUM and SMART_CONSENSUS stay off — evidence clear.
riskFlags: ELITE_FOLLOW is copying wallet 'aenews2' which has 44% win rate — this wallet should be blacklisted or deprioritized within the engine configuration
$500 open position on Minnesota Twins is 6% of current equity on a single game — even if likely to win, this concentration should not recur under new maxEventExposure cap
Stop-loss pattern on Philadelphia Phillies (two separate bets, both stop-lossed on same day) suggests correlated event risk — same-event multi-bet exposure should be reviewed at code level

Win rate on SHORT_FAVORITE is strong but PnL is negative: implies edge exists but sizing/exit mechanics are capturing less EV than expected — worth auditing stop-loss threshold and max-hold exit logic
15% drawdown from inception is approaching a threshold where strategy validity should be formally re-examined if losses continue to -20%
